definition: a) Extreme-survival case-control (>=85/90/95 y, 90th/99th percentile, centenarians vs younger controls)
what_it_detects: Alleles whose frequency differs between survivors to a high age and younger/never-long-lived controls; integrates all mortality up to the threshold; strongest single-variant signals at the 99th percentile (Deelen 2019).
blind_spots_biases: Small case numbers (thousands); controls are often alive younger people, so variants acting before the control age are invisible and cohort/birth-year allele drift confounds; cannot say at what age the variant acted; centenarian selection mixes "absence of risk" with true protection; ancestry-specific (APOE/FOXO3 weak in Taiwan, Hsieh 2026); survivor bias for sex-specific loci (HLA-DRB1*15:01 men only).
loci_found: APOE e4/e2, FOXO3, 5q33.3 (rs2149954), GPR78, CDKN2A/B (99th, suggestive), IL6 rs2069837 and ANKRD20A9P (Han Chinese), HLA-DRB1*15:01 (male), ZNF806/NUAK1 etc. (Taiwan)
recommended_use_in_v2: SCORE (primary). Store percentile threshold and control age in studies.csv; weight 99th-percentile evidence as the most specific "longevity" signal.

definition: b) Parental-lifespan / family-proxy GWAS (kin-cohort, Martingale residuals, parents' attained age, both parents top 10%)
what_it_detects: Per-allele effect on parental hazard (years of life per allele, x2 to convert to self); very large N (~1M parents) gives most of the 20-30 known loci; age-band stratification possible (Timmers 2019 bands; Joshi 2016 <75 vs >=75).
blind_spots_biases: Parents dying <40 excluded and many parents still alive (right-censored), so late effects are underpowered (e.g., 1,853 paternal deaths at 90-120 y vs 84,545 at 70-80 y in Timmers 2019 source data); effect diluted by 50% kinship; cohort effects of parents born early 20th century (smoking era inflates CHRNA3/5); misreport of parental age; mixes genetic with shared environment; dominated by common midlife killers (CVD, smoking, dementia).
loci_found: APOE, CHRNA3/5, CDKN2B-AS1, LPA, HLA-DQA1/DRB1, SH2B3/ATXN2, FURIN/FES, ZW10, PSORS1C3, 13q21.31, ABO, ZC3HC1, IGF2R, LDLR, CELSR2/PSRC1, MAGI3, KCNK3, HTT, FOXO3, 5q33.3, MC2R (top-10% only), EPHX2
recommended_use_in_v2: SCORE (primary). Always flag PROXY:PARENTAL; record age bands where available; treat as weaker evidence for LATE effects.

definition: c) Own-survival hazard (Cox) in prospective cohorts / biobanks
what_it_detects: HR for death in genotyped individuals; can test age interactions directly and censor intermediate diseases (Wolters 2019: e4 HR 1.17 attenuated to 1.07 after censoring dementia).
blind_spots_biases: Few deaths in biobanks recruited at 40-70 (UKB 35,551 deaths in Park 2025), so signals are dominated by early, cancer-driven deaths; follow-up covers a narrow age window; healthy-volunteer bias; disease-specific survival loci barely overlap susceptibility loci (Yang 2025).
loci_found: APOE, ZSCAN23 (common); BRCA1/2, ATM, TET2, ASXL1, CKMT1B (LoF burden, life-shortening); PRS for SBP and BMI
recommended_use_in_v2: SCORE (supporting); preferred source for age-interaction claims and for LIFELONG classification.

definition: d) Healthspan / disease-free survival and multivariate ageing factors (healthspan GWAS, MANOVA, aging-GIP1, mvAge genomic SEM)
what_it_detects: Loci shared by healthspan, lifespan, longevity, frailty, self-rated health and clocks; more power than any single trait; finds non-disease loci (FOXO3, FGD6, ZW10, SLC4A7, LINC02513, HTT, MAML3).
blind_spots_biases: Healthspan = first of a list of diseases (Zenin: 7 conditions incl. cancer) so it counts non-fatal events (skin cancer, pigmentation loci IRF4/TYR/DEF8) and is censored at UKB ages (<~80); composite factors inherit the inputs' sample overlap and weighting; a factor locus need not affect lifespan; frailty/self-rated health import behaviour/SES loci.
loci_found: Zenin: APOE, LPA, HLA class II (rs1049053), IRF4, TYR, DEF8, FGFR2, CDKN2B-AS1...; Timmers 2020: FOXO3, SLC4A7, LINC02513, ZW10, FGD6, LPA, LDLR, CDKN2B-AS1, TOX3, APOE; aging-GIP1: 27 regions incl. HTT, MAML3; mvAge: 38 loci incl. TCF7L2, PABPC4
recommended_use_in_v2: SCORE only when the locus also has a lifespan-type signal (a, b or c) at least suggestive; otherwise ANNOTATE with label HEALTHSPAN_ONLY.

definition: e) Age-dependent allele-frequency change in cross-sectional cohorts (viability selection)
what_it_detects: Alleles whose frequency declines with age among the living or with parental age at death; intrinsically gives an age-of-action profile (e4 decline from ~70 y; CHRNA3 decline across all paternal ages).
blind_spots_biases: Confounded by birth-cohort ancestry drift and recruitment bias (needs ancestry/batch null model); power depends on where the change occurs (Mostafavi: ~20/90/60% power for change starting at 20/50/70 y); only very large effects reach genome-wide significance (only APOE and CHRNA3 found).
loci_found: APOE e4 (rs6857, rs769449), CHRNA3 (rs1051730), MEOX2 rs4721453 (sensitivity analysis); trait-PGS signals (puberty timing, cholesterol, CAD, BMI, asthma)
recommended_use_in_v2: SCORE (supporting/confirmatory) and PRIMARY SOURCE for age_of_action; never sole evidence.

definition: f) Familial longevity scores (FEL, LRC/mLRC) and long-lived families (LLS, LLFS)
what_it_detects: Heritable longevity: transmitted only when top-10% survivors cluster (>=20% of relatives long-lived); selects cases with less phenocopy; family members have >10 y delayed first chronic disease.
blind_spots_biases: Is a case-selection device rather than a variant test; small samples; requires multigeneration genealogy; enriched for specific populations (Utah, Netherlands, Ashkenazi); results feed back into (a) or (g).
loci_found: Few single loci; LLS: lower CAD PGS and cholesterol-metabolism PGS
recommended_use_in_v2: ANNOTATE (study design attribute in studies.csv); evidence from such studies is scored under EXTREME_SURVIVAL_CC with a FAMILIAL flag that up-weights specificity.

definition: g) Depletion of disease-risk alleles / low polygenic disease burden in the long-lived
what_it_detects: Whether long-lived people simply lack common disease risk alleles ("absence of risk"); informed scans (iGWAS, Bayesian priors) boost power using disease GWAS.
blind_spots_biases: Results conflict by disease and design: no global depletion for CAD/cancer/T2D alleles in Leiden nonagenarians (Beekman 2010) and no pathogenic-variant depletion in Ashkenazi centenarians (Gutman 2020), but CAD PGS lower with more long-lived ancestors (Sant'Anna 2026), AD protective PGS higher in centenarians (Bae 2026); circular if disease loci are then re-scored as longevity loci.
loci_found: Mainly polygenic (CAD, AD, SBP, BMI, cholesterol); single loci only via informed scans (CDKN2B-AS1, ATXN2/SH2B3, LPA ...)
recommended_use_in_v2: ANNOTATE (label ABSENCE_OF_RISK); do not create new pro-longevity rows from disease GWAS alone - route to disease modules.

definition: h) Rare protective loss-of-function ("human knockouts") and gene-burden tests
what_it_detects: Gene-level effects of PTV/missense burden on lifespan; rare protective alleles in centenarians (IGF1R, mTOR, IIS/AMPK, Wnt); drug-target-like LoF with lifelong biomarker lowering (PCSK9, LPA, APOC3).
blind_spots_biases: Large-N burden tests find mainly life-SHORTENING genes (BRCA1/2, ATM, TET2) driven by cancer and clonal haematopoiesis; pro-longevity rare variants come from small centenarian exomes and are unreplicated; protective LoF evidence is usually for disease, not lifespan; somatic CHIP mimics germline in blood-derived exomes.
loci_found: Shortening: BRCA1, BRCA2, ATM, TET2, ASXL1, CKMT1B; candidate protective: IGF1R, RPS6, FLCN, SIK3, RWDD1, Wnt-pathway genes; disease-protective LoF: PCSK9, LPA, APOC3
recommended_use_in_v2: ANNOTATE for pro-longevity rare variants (tier C-D unless replicated); life-shortening burden genes belong in disease modules (negatives/cross-links).

definition: i) Evolutionary / selection-based (antagonistic pleiotropy, mutation accumulation, balancing selection, comparative genomics)
what_it_detects: Why risk alleles persist (early-life fitness benefit, late cost); predicts which loci should be trade-offs and age-specific; comparative constraint across mammals.
blind_spots_biases: Not a variant-level test of human lifespan; population-genetic signals are confounded by demography; comparative genomics works at gene level; many claims rest on single cohorts (Ghana APOE fertility).
loci_found: APOE e4 (fertility/infection), CAD loci with reproductive pleiotropy, reproduction PGS
recommended_use_in_v2: ANNOTATE only (pleiotropy label AP; supports TRADEOFF and AGE_INVERTING hypotheses).

definition: j) Causal / Mendelian-randomization definitions (variant as proxy for a modifiable mediator)
what_it_detects: Variants whose lifespan effect is explained by a causal risk factor (LDL, Lp(a), BP, BMI, smoking, education, VCAM1); defines actionability.
blind_spots_biases: A pro-longevity allele here is "lower exposure"; horizontal pleiotropy; MR assumes lifelong linear effects so says nothing about age at action; weak instruments for protein targets.
loci_found: LPA/apo(a), VCAM1, LDLR, PCSK9, CELSR2/SORT1, CHRNA3/5 (smoking), BP and BMI PGS
recommended_use_in_v2: ANNOTATE (modifiable_mediator, actionability); allows the score of a locus to be qualified but not created.

definition: k) Biomarker-anchored (slower epigenetic/proteomic clock, telomere length)
what_it_detects: Variants associated with slower biological-age measures; large N; mechanistic hypotheses (TERT, GDF15).
blind_spots_biases: Clock acceleration is not lifespan: TERT telomere-lengthening alleles raise IEAA (Lu 2018); clocks capture smoking/adiposity/SES; proteomic clocks are dominated by exposome; direction can conflict with mortality.
loci_found: TERT (IEAA), ~137 DNAm-clock loci; CDKN2A/B rs2184061 (GDF15 signature); CETP I405V (lipoprotein size)
recommended_use_in_v2: ANNOTATE only (BIOMARKER label); never contributes to pro-longevity score.
